taoist.name: Box Breathing 4-4-4-4
taoist.effect: Four equal phases create a perfect yin-yang rhythm. Harmonizes qi, calms the nervous system, brings equanimity. Foundation of Taoist meditation.
taoist.instructions: Four equal phases of 4 seconds. Inhale · Full retention · Exhale · Empty. Observe the silence in the spaces between the movements of the air.
taoist.doneSub: Qi flows. Yin and yang in balance.

quadrada6.name: Box Breathing 6-6-6-6
quadrada6.effect: Same box structure with longer counts. Deepens attention and inner silence. Good when the 4s practice is already established.
quadrada6.instructions: Four equal phases of 6 seconds. Inhale · Full retention · Exhale · Empty. Allow each phase to deepen naturally.

quadrada8.name: Box Breathing 8-8-8-8
quadrada8.effect: Advanced level. Long retention and extended emptiness create states of deep stillness. Requires prior practice with shorter versions.
quadrada8.instructions: Four equal phases of 8 seconds. Inhale · Full retention · Exhale · Empty. Practice only if the shorter versions are already comfortable.
quadrada8.doneSub: Stillness has settled. The body found its center.

quadrada10.name: Box Breathing 10-10-10-10
quadrada10.effect: Deep contemplative practice. Each cycle lasts 40 seconds. Only for those who have the previous versions well established in the body.
quadrada10.instructions: Four equal phases of 10 seconds. Each cycle lasts 40 seconds. Only for experienced practitioners. Inhale · Retention · Exhale · Empty with full attention.

prolongada3.name: Extended Exhale
prolongada3.effect: Entry-level version. Exhaling twice the length of the inhale gently activates the vagus nerve. A good gateway for those who don't yet practice controlled breathing.
prolongada3.instructions: Inhale softly through the nose for 3 seconds. Exhale slowly through the nose for 6 seconds — twice the time. Entry version, gentle and accessible.
prolongada3.doneSub: The vagus nerve calms. The anchor is cast.

prolongada.name: Extended Exhale
prolongada.effect: Exhaling twice the length of the inhale activates the vagus nerve and slows the heart. Immediate anchor in turbulent moments. Entry version.
prolongada.instructions: Inhale softly through the nose for 4 seconds. Exhale slowly through the nose for 8 seconds — twice the time. Can be done in any position, at any moment.
prolongada.doneSub: The vagus nerve calms. The anchor is cast.

prolongada6.name: Extended Exhale
prolongada6.effect: Deepened version. The longer exhale intensifies vagal activation and creates an even more stable calm. For when the body already knows the 4-8 rhythm.
prolongada6.instructions: Inhale softly through the nose for 6 seconds. Exhale slowly through the nose for 12 seconds. Deepened version — the longer exhale intensifies vagal activation and creates more stable calm.
prolongada6.doneSub: The vagus nerve responds deeply. Stable calm.

farinelli.name: Farinelli Breathing
farinelli.effect: Attributed to Farinelli and Porpora's method. Six progressive levels train the appoggio — active support without tension. At higher counts, the inhale is taken in plateaus: Lamperti's thimble breathing.
farinelli.instructions: Six progressive levels from 5 to 10 counts, after Richard Miller (The Structure of Singing). Inhale — Suspend — Exhale, always symmetrical. At higher counts, the inhale happens in plateaus: micro-suspensions within the inhalation phase itself, without exhaling. This is Lamperti's thimble breathing. Active appoggio, no visible tension in neck or shoulders.
farinelli.doneSub: The appoggio is active. The air column, sustained.

jufranco1.name: Exercise 1
jufranco1.effect: Inhale for 6 counts, release controlled airflow (S or x) for 6 counts, release. Introduction to airflow management.
jufranco1.instructions: Inhale for 6 counts. Release controlled airflow as S or x for 6 counts. Release. The S or x is a continuous fricative — not apnea, it is air in controlled motion.
jufranco1.doneSub: The air column found its flow.

jufranco2.name: Exercise 2
jufranco2.sub: Inhale · airflow · hold · airflow · release — 6 counts
jufranco2.effect: Adds a suspension between airflows. Trains breath suspension and return to flow control.
jufranco2.timerSub: Inhale · airflow · hold · airflow · release — 6 counts
jufranco2.instructions: Inhale for 6 counts. S or x for 6. Hold for 6 — active suspension, not collapse. S or x for 6. Release. Trains returning to flow after suspension.

jufranco3.name: Exercise 3
jufranco3.sub: Inhale · airflow · hold · airflow · hold · release — 6 counts
jufranco3.effect: More complex version with two suspensions. Maximum airflow control across multiple suspended gestures before the final release.
jufranco3.timerSub: Inhale · airflow · hold · airflow · hold · release — 6 counts
jufranco3.instructions: Inhale for 6 counts. S or x for 6. Hold for 6. S or x for 6. Hold for 6. Release. Maximum airflow control across multiple suspended gestures. Requires the previous versions well incorporated in the body.
jufranco3.doneSub: The air column, mastered. The instrument, ready.

bhramari.name: Bhramari
bhramari.effect: Inhale and on the exhale produce a soft, continuous hum. The vibration resonates through the skull and directly activates the vagus nerve. Deeply calming, reduces anxiety and blood pressure.
bhramari.instructions: Inhale through the nose for 4 seconds. Gently close the ears with the thumbs and eyes with the fingers. On the exhale, produce a soft continuous hum — like a bee — for as long as comfortable, up to 12 seconds. Feel the vibration resonating through the skull and chest.
bhramari.doneSub: The vibration calms. The nervous system found its center.

nadishodhana.name: Nadi Shodhana
nadishodhana.effect: Balances the brain hemispheres and subtle and physical channels. Mental clarity, deep calm. Excellent for starting the day with full centeredness.
nadishodhana.instructions: Right hand: thumb closes right nostril, ring finger closes left nostril. Inhale left 4s → retention 4s → exhale right 8s. Then inhale right 4s → retention 4s → exhale left 8s. That is 1 complete cycle.
nadishodhana.doneSub: The channels are clear. Balance restored.

tanden.name: Tanden Kokyu
tanden.effect: Directs breath to the tanden — center of force 3 fingers below the navel. Deep grounding, serenity, emotional stability.
tanden.instructions: Spine erect. Attention to the tanden — 3 fingers below the navel. Inhale expanding the abdomen like a bowl. Exhale slowly, letting the center gently draw inward.
tanden.doneSub: The center is firm. The mind, still.

chandrabhedana.name: Chandra Bhedana
chandrabhedana.effect: Activates the lunar channel (ida nadi). Refreshes the body, calms the agitated mind. Antidote for anxiety and excessive internal heat.
chandrabhedana.instructions: Close the right nostril with the thumb. Inhale through the left nostril (lunar, feminine). Close the left with the ring finger, exhale through the right.
chandrabhedana.doneSub: The moon calms. The system refreshes.

nestor.name: 5.5 Breathing
nestor.effect: The rhythm of 5.5 breaths per minute is identified by Nestor as ideal for humans — synchronizes heart, lungs and nervous system with maximum precision.
nestor.instructions: Inhale softly through the nose for 5.5 seconds, expanding the abdomen. Exhale softly through the nose for 5.5 seconds. Do not force — just flow. This is the rhythm science identifies as ideal for humans.
nestor.doneSub: The perfect rhythm. The body found its natural tempo.

coherent.name: Cardiac Coherence
coherent.effect: The rhythm of 5–6 breaths per minute synchronizes heart, brain and respiratory system. Reduces anxiety, stabilizes mood. Can be done in any position.
coherent.instructions: Inhale softly through the nose for 5 seconds. Exhale softly for 5 seconds. Do not force — just flow. The rhythm synchronizes heart, lungs and brain.
coherent.doneSub: Coherence restored. Heart and mind speak the same language.

478.name: 4-7-8 Breathing
478.effect: The long retention and extended exhale activate the vagus nerve and parasympathetic system. Rapidly reduces cortisol. Excellent after waking tense or anxious.
478.instructions: Exhale all air. Inhale through the nose counting 4. Hold counting 7. Exhale completely through the mouth counting 8. The ratio is what matters.
478.doneSub: The vagus nerve responds. Cortisol recedes.

anapana.name: Anapanasati
anapana.effect: The technique taught by the Buddha: simply observe the natural breath, without control. The timer marks total time. Cultivates presence, non-attachment and equanimity.
anapana.instructions: Don't control anything. Just observe the air entering and leaving through the nostrils. When the mind wanders, gently return. The timer marks the time — the breath is yours.
anapana.doneSub: The breath is the teacher. The mind has learned to listen.

sushumna.name: Central Channel
sushumna.effect: Visualize energy rising up the spine as you inhale, resting at the crown during retention, and descending serenely on the exhale. Body-mind integration.
sushumna.instructions: Visualize a channel of light along the spine. Inhale feeling energy rise from the base to the crown of the head. Retain at the apex. Exhale descending with serenity.
sushumna.doneSub: The central channel, illuminated. Body and mind, integrated.

kapalabhati.name: Kapalabhati
kapalabhati.effect: Rapid exhales through the nose. Awakens, cleanses, warms.
kapalabhati.instructions: Sit upright. Contract the abdomen to exhale forcefully through the nose. The inhale is passive and automatic. Keep the face relaxed.

bhastrika.name: Bhastrika
bhastrika.effect: Forceful inhale and exhale. Activates the sympathetic nervous system.
bhastrika.instructions: Inhale forcefully filling the chest, exhale forcefully emptying it. Vigorous and controlled rhythm. Pause 30s between rounds.

ujjayi.name: Ujjayi
ujjayi.effect: Breathing with oceanic sound. Focus, presence, internal warmth.
ujjayi.instructions: Inhale through the nose gently contracting the glottis — oceanic sound. Exhale through the nose with the same soft sound. Feel the internal warmth expanding.

suryabhedana.name: Surya Bhedana
suryabhedana.effect: Right nostril only (solar). Energizes, warms, activates.
suryabhedana.instructions: Close the left nostril with the ring finger. Inhale slowly through the right nostril. Close the right with the thumb, exhale through the left.
suryabhedana.doneSub: The inner sun has been activated.

wimhof.name: Wim Hof Breathing
wimhof.effect: 30 deep rapid breaths, then exhale fully and hold — each round retention grows naturally. Activates the nervous system, increases stress tolerance.
wimhof.instructions: Lie down or sit comfortably. 30 deep rapid breaths, then exhale fully and hold. Press "breathe in" when you need to. 3 rounds with progressive goals.
wimhof.doneSub: Nervous system activated and reset. Clear mind.
